newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico's 'Virgin of Metro' finds a brighter home.
newsitem.headline: Mexico's 'Virgin of Metro' finds a brighter home.

text.p: A stain on pavement that has been revered by some Mexicans as resembling Mexico's Virgin of Guadalupe was moved above ground on Tuesday and blessed by church officials in front of hundreds of devotees.

Bearing flowers and candles, Mexicans lined up to touch the glass-fronted shrine to Mexico's newest religious icon -- the so-called "Virgin of the Metro" which was discovered by a cleaner mopping up the subway on June 1.

For almost two months, thousands of visitors have flocked to the dank Hidalgo subway station in Mexico City to pay homage to what they swore was a miraculous image of the Virgin of Guadalupe, Mexico's revered patron saint.
Metro officials dug up the stones on which the postcard-sized stain appeared, and placed them behind glass in a nearby park.
To many, it was a modern-day evocation of the appearance of the image of the Virgin Mary, known in Mexico as the Virgin of Guadalupe, on the tunic of Mexican peasant Juan Diego in 1531.
Mariachi musicians crooned traditional love songs to the shrine, and dozens of worshippers -- from tearful Indian women to businessmen in suits -- joined in.
"If miracles happen, they don't have to have happened years ago," said Hugo Figueroa, a local devotee. "People can believe it or not, but it's a crystal clear figure of the Virgin of Guadalupe."
"I asked her for many things, above all peace in the whole world," an elderly worshipper, Salvador Lozano, said.
